title: Nasi Goreng
subtitle: Indonesian fried rice with sweet soy sauce and fried egg
excerpt: Nasi goreng is Indonesia's national dish -- fried rice with a deep, dark coating of kecap manis sweet soy sauce. It is eaten at any time of day, often topped with a fried egg. It is quick to make with leftover rice and keeps the flavour direct and bold.
sourceNotes: Nasi goreng (fried rice) is considered one of Indonesia's national dishes. The use of kecap manis -- a sweet, thick soy sauce invented in Java -- distinguishes it from Chinese fried rice. The dish is eaten across Indonesia, Malaysia, and the Netherlands (through colonial connections). It is listed among the most delicious foods in the world by CNN readers.

content.text: Nasi goreng is one of the most satisfying things you can make with leftover rice. The key is high heat and cold, day-old rice -- fresh rice turns mushy. Kecap manis gives the dish its signature dark colour and sweet depth. This comes together in under 20 minutes.

items.prepNote: cooked and cooled -- day-old rice is best
fry 1 egg per person as a topping
use kecap manis (sweet soy sauce) -- it is thicker and sweeter than regular soy
use regular soy sauce -- adds saltiness alongside the kecap manis

content.text: Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a wok or large frying pan over the highest heat possible. Fry the shallots and garlic for 1 to 2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the carrot and cabbage. Stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add the prawns and toss for 1 minute.
Add the cold rice. Break up any clumps with a spoon. Stir-fry for 3 minutes until the rice is hot.
Add the kecap manis, regular soy sauce, and chilli flakes. Toss until the rice is evenly coated -- it will turn a deep brown colour.
In a separate pan, fry an egg per person in a little oil until the white is set and the yolk still runny. Serve the nasi goreng topped with the fried egg and spring onion.

items.symptom: Rice is mushy and sticking together
items.cause: Rice too fresh or too wet
items.fix: Use cold, day-old rice. If using freshly cooked rice, spread it on a tray and chill for 2 hours. The kecap manis adds moisture -- if the rice is already wet, this makes it stodgy.

content.text: Nasi goreng is eaten throughout Indonesia at any hour. Street vendors (warungs) sell it from dawn. In Dutch homes it is a legacy of colonial connection. The fried egg on top is not optional in Indonesia -- it is part of the dish. Kecap manis is the ingredient that makes nasi goreng distinctively Indonesian.
